facts: No. On Windows Mobium drives Android only; iOS is not possible there.
Mobium drives iOS through xcrun simctl and WebDriverAgent, and a real iPhone needs WebDriverAgent built and signed by xcodebuild and reached over CoreDevice's tunnel — all of which are macOS-only.
Nor through another machine: --remote, which drives a Mac's devices over SSH, needs a Unix socket on the caller's side and refuses on Windows.
note: WINDOWS.md answers the local case. The remote case is the obvious follow-up and has its own answer: cmd/mobium/remote_windows.go:15-16 refuses (SETUP 'Driving another machine's devices': 'on Windows --remote refuses, and says so'), so ADD that section, which retrieval ranked third.
ask: Is 'iOS from Windows through --remote to a Mac' something you want planned (a named-pipe or TCP forward on Windows), or does 'refuses' stay the answer? The question's gold is right either way today.
